raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not chase fancy methods. I farm the way that keeps the land steady and the cash flow safe. On my 4.1 mu, I will still keep most land in the wheat-maize cycle, because that is the most familiar and it feeds the household first. Cotton I will keep on a small piece for cash income, but I will not expand it because cotton takes more watching and more pesticide, and with only two people at home I cannot spread myself too thin.

For wheat, I will put about 3.1 mu into winter wheat, then follow it with summer maize on the same land. Wheat is the base crop here, and with well water I do not want to cut inputs too hard. The extension fellow says not to overdo nitrogen, but from my own years I know if wheat looks weak in spring, yield drops fast, so I still give a solid base fertilizer and one topdressing. Maize goes in right after wheat harvest, fast and simple, because that turnaround is tight and I do not have time for heavy tillage. Cotton I will keep at 1 mu. Cotton can bring money, but it needs more labor and more spraying, so at my age I only keep a little. I would rather be a bit conservative than risk a bad year from saving too much on fertilizer or water.

decision.reasoning_summary: I keep most of my land in wheat and maize because that is the safest and most familiar way for my family. I still keep a little cotton for cash, but not too much because it needs more labor and spraying. I use well irrigation, so I will water the wheat a few times and maize once if rain is short. I do not push the fertilizer to the highest level, but I also do not cut too much, because after so many years I know being too stingy can lose more yield than the fertilizer saves in money.
